findings.current: I know when I can stretch my legs.
findings.defect: This does not convey the Korean idiom’s point: he assesses the situation before acting and does not overreach. The current wording suggests knowing when he can relax or extend his legs.
findings.rationale: “누울 자리는 보고 발을 뻗습니다” means to judge the circumstances before acting.
findings.replacement: I may look reckless, but I know when to pick my battles.

findings.current: People were haggling at what looked like a market on one side of the street.
findings.defect: “The street” adds a specific location not established in the source.
findings.rationale: The Korean says only that a market seemed to be underway “on one side”; it does not mention a street.
findings.replacement: People were haggling at what looked like a market on one side.

findings.current: Namho and I exchanged a look before I asked, “Did you study Han Chinese?”
findings.defect: The exchange loses the source’s indication that their glance was meaningful or knowing.
findings.rationale: The source says they exchanged “의미심장한 눈빛,” a meaningful or significant look.
findings.replacement: Namho and I exchanged a meaningful look before I asked, “Did you study Han Chinese?”

summary: The chapter is broadly faithful, but one idiom loses its meaning and two smaller details are altered or omitted.
